text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Costas Simitis wants a government with new brains. Ankara believes the election results can have a positive effect on Greco-Turkish relations.
- Arrests of Omonia football club fans are expected after Sunday's match violence.
- Boats will take water from Turkey to the occupied areas.
CYPRUS MAIL
- The United Nations reported at least six shooting incidents along the buffer zone in the last three days.
- Hooligans mar the start of the soccer season.
- Broad welcome in Cyprus for Simitis poll victory.
- Cyprus Airways pilots union claims one of their members is being 'victimised' by management.
HARAVGHI
- Costas Simitis is preparing changes in the government.
- One hundred and fifty contract workers in the civil service want permanent jobs.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- The post-election scene is being created in Greece. A crucial start with many changes.
- Unemployed Turkish Cypriots will recieve six million pounds in benefits.
- Chemicals which have been banned by the government for being dangerous have been used in the breeding of pigs.
SIMERINI
- Day after Greek elections sparks intensive consultations for the winners and losers.
- Limassol Mayor Antonis Haggipavlou will announce in the next few days whether he will run in municipal elections in December.
